authorization.reason: Loop 31 has no executed sensor-dependence result, current S21 and consumed S7 evidence do not provide a fresh synchronized complete peripheral-control set, and planning research is not consent, acquisition, data access, model, or claim authorization.

decision.research_question: Can future predictive information attributed to EEG or MEG remain after target leakage, timing, key identity, ocular, muscular, motion, audio, environmental, and prompt shortcuts are measured under one synchronized protocol?

existing_evidence_inventory.finding: Brain2Qwerty v1 uses 500 ms EEG or MEG windows aligned from 200 ms before to 300 ms after known keypresses and reports motor and keyboard-layout structure, so its result is overt prompted typing rather than no-keypress language production.

Brain2Qwerty v2 removes explicit keypress alignment at inference but still records healthy volunteers physically typing after audio prompts with keypress-locked minimal visual feedback; it explicitly leaves patient operation without actual keypresses for future validation.

The working S21 sentence path uses 102 magnetometers and STI101-derived timing. The committed cache and reports do not carry synchronized EOG, EMG, gaze, hand motion, microphone, or body-motion streams for a complete Loop 35 comparison.

The source S7 BrainVision bundle names three ocular channels that were excluded from the 61-channel EEG cache, but the evaluation is consumed and exclusion does not prove the remaining scalp channels are free of ocular or muscle information.
The cross-session S21 MEG model and within-session S7 EEG classifier were both worse than no-signal priors, so no positive local result currently reaches the Loop 35 attribution question.
Loop 31 can at most establish sensor-signal dependence and explicitly requires Loop 35 before stronger origin wording.

Small task-specific eye movements supported persistent MEG decoding in a visual working-memory study, demonstrating that above-chance sensor decoding can track behavior outside the intended neural representation.

Simultaneous EEG/EMG movement work found artifact components could be more informative to classifiers, while synchronized MEG/EMG/audio/head-position speech recordings showed task-linked movement and muscle artifacts can distort MEG.

claim_boundary: This registry closes Loop 35 planning research only; it is not a preregistration, authorization, fixture, acquisition, model run, confound result, or brain-specific claim.
No protected signal, cache, target, prompt, typed response, checkpoint, model, EOG, gaze, EMG, motion, audio, keyboard, device, stream, S20, S25, or hardware operation occurred.
The current S21 and consumed S7 paths can cite timing and channel metadata but cannot provide a fresh complete synchronized peripheral-control comparison.
A channel called EEG or MEG and an artifact-rejected signal do not by themselves prove that predictive information originates in the brain.

The maximum future local result is incremental brain-sensor information beyond every recorded peripheral and timing comparator for the exact people, task, device, streams, and partitions; unrecorded confounds remain unresolved.

No absolute brain origin, language-intent decoding, no-keypress or attempted-movement transfer, patient benefit, population generalization, real-time behavior, portable hardware, at-home use, arbitrary-thought typing, assistive efficacy, diagnostic use, clinical claim, or product-safety claim is established.
